**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat conjunction-linked suffixes as bounds**

When `以上` or `以下` is introduced by the common conjunctions `及` or `或`, this suffix grammar no longer attaches the qualifier to the amount. Both `normalizeMoneyValueV4('4000元及以上')` and a cropped `4000元` candidate quoted from `王甲工资4000元或以下` return `exact` with `4000.00`, so a lower or upper bound can become an exact production amount. Allow the bounded conjunction before these suffixes while retaining the existing ordinary-prose continuation guards.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept 个月 as a monthly rate denominator**

Common monthly-rate forms using the explicit classifier `个`, such as `4000元每个月` and `4000元/个月` (and traditional `每個月`), are classified as unsupported because the captured denominator must begin directly with `月`. The otherwise equivalent `4000元每月` and `4000元/月` remain exact, so a valid candidate declared with `meaning: "rate"` and `rateUnit: "month"` loses its amount solely because of this ordinary unit spelling. Recognize the complete `个月`/`個月` alias without accepting longer words such as `月份` or `月亮`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept classifier and ordinal recurring payment dates**

When a payment schedule uses the common forms `每个月15日`, `每個月十五號`, or `每月第15日`, this exact regex rejects the date while `每月15日` passes. Runtime ingestion consequently adds `source_relation_unresolved` to an otherwise explicit `payment_date`, preventing it from being used; allow the optional `个/個` classifier and `第` within the same validated 1–31 day grammar.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse fullwidth bare amounts after RMB symbols**

Fresh evidence beyond the repaired fullwidth yuan-token cases is that `normalizeMoneyValueV4('￥４０００')` and `normalizeMoneyValueV4('¥４０００')` still return `unsupported` with no amount, although `￥4000` and `人民币４０００` both return exact `4000.00`. The symbol-prefixed token alternative requires a yuan tail, so these unambiguous currency-marked values fall through to the legacy ASCII-only bare-number parser; admit fullwidth digits on this complete symbol-prefixed path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept traditional spellings of the one-time payment suffix**

Fresh evidence beyond the repaired simplified `一并支付` continuation is that `4000元一並支付`, `4000元一併支付`, and their `給付`/`發放` variants still normalize as `unsupported`, while `4000元一并支付` remains exact. Because the numeral-leading suffix is treated as a truncated amount unless this exception matches, add the traditional `並/併` spellings to the bounded payment-instruction grammar.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept explicit calendar wage-payment events**

For a concrete payment event such as `王甲工资于2026年1月15日支付` or `王甲工资在2026年1月15日发放`, the point-date branch accepts only `收到/领取`, while payment verbs are accepted only for recurring dates or deadlines. The resulting `payment_date` receives `source_relation_unresolved` even though the source directly binds the worker, wage, date, and payment action; add a bounded point-date payment layout without treating it as proof of receipt.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize explicit other-money nouns during attribution**

When the source directly states an `other_money` receipt using the nouns required by the extraction contract, such as `王甲收到经济补偿金4000元`, `王甲收到赔偿金4000元`, or `甲公司收到材料款4000元`, this finite role grammar rejects the relationship and runtime ingestion adds `source_relation_unresolved`. The same layout passes when the noun is merely `补偿`, so extend the bounded role vocabulary to the supported compensation, bonus, fee, deposit, fine, and material-payment nouns rather than forcing these explicit owner/value events into manual review.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
